subject.title: [Feature]: Audio file support in read tool (multimodal parity with images)

question: Should OpenClaw make native audio a first-class read-tool and LLM content type, or keep `read()` text/image-only and route audio through media-understanding/transcription workflows?
rationale: The requested behavior changes provider payload shape, local-file egress, model capability checks, fallback behavior, and session/transcript persistence, so code inspection cannot choose the product/security contract by itself.

options.title: Design shared native-audio contract first
options.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, model capability gating, payload limits, security/audit behavior, and transcript persistence before implementing read-tool audio parity.

options.title: Fold under broader native-audio tracker
options.body: Keep this issue linked to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51667 and require that broader native-audio design to explicitly cover local `read()` audio files before this can close.

options.title: Keep read text/image-only
options.body: Decline native audio for `read()` and document audio files as transcription or media-understanding inputs instead.

recommendation.title: Design shared native-audio contract first
recommendation.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider serialization, model capability gating, payload limits, security/audit behavior, and transcript persistence before implementing read-tool audio parity.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current provenance across the read tool, LLM content shape, media MIME handling, and media-understanding contracts that this decision would change.
